body: The material `MatDrawerContainer` reproduces this by [subscribing](https://github.com/angular/material2/blob/5.1.1/src/lib/sidenav/drawer.ts#L482) to the [Directionality.change](https://github.com/angular/material2/blob/5.1.1/src/cdk/bidi/directionality.ts#L42) output.

Here's an example using material: http://plnkr.co/edit/RvLCnqc1yKc1tX8LKqop

Each time you toggle the `mat-drawer-container` it leaks the subscription mentioned above which references the `MatDrawerContainer` which references more etc. Click the button a few times, take a heap snapshot and search for "MatDrawerContainer"...

Here's a potential fix + tests: https://github.com/jbedard/angular/commit/30e07b3fb78848af008320c7053d2777982e589b

This changes the `isAsync` handling to be at emit-time instead of subscriber-handler time. I was hoping to avoid such a change but I can't figure out how to fix this issue and keep `isAsync` support for the case where `subscribe(generator)` is used. One benefit (I think?) is that subscribers are no longer wrapped which I often find minorly annoying when debugging or inspecting stack traces.

An alternative might be using a scheduler? But it appears that schedulers do not make complete/error async which would be a breaking change.

EDIT: I just realized this commit changes listeners from independent async events to being grouped per-`emit`. This could potentially be a good thing (less CD?), but probably makes this option a breaking change. Probably also means some tests are missing...
